newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-WEST INDIES SCORE ENCOURAGING WIN.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-WEST INDIES SCORE ENCOURAGING WIN.

text.p: A century by opening batsman Sherwin Campbell on Sunday helped West Indies polish off their preparations for next week's third test against Australia with a six-wicket defeat of Victoria.
Campbell was 112 not out as West Indies reached 219 for four in their second innings midway through the final day of the four-day match after being set a winning target of 216.
The form of Campbell will be encouraging for West Indies as they go into the third test after heavy losses in the first two matches against Australia.

Campbell notched a century in the first test in Brisbane last month and has scored two of the three hundreds recorded so far on tour by West Indies. Shivnarine Chanderpaul, who missed the match against Victoria, scored the first on tour with 123 against Western Australia last month.
West Indies resumed on 41 for one with Campbell and number three batsman Brian Lara both on 14.

Lara went on to make 46 before falling to leg-spinner Brad Stacey for 46 as West Indies lost three wickets in the morning session. Stacey had seen Lara take 33 from just two of his overs in the first innings.

Robert Samuels and Carl Hooper were both dismissed cheaply, while Jimmy Adams was unbeaten with Campbell on 20 at the close. Lara, the world record-holder for the highest scores in test and first-class cricket, was denied his first century of the tour when he was controversially dismissed hit wicket for 86 in the first innings.

While the West Indies' batsmen showed more resolve than they had during a seven-match losing streak earlier on tour, their bowlers set up the win. Pacemen Kenneth Benjamin and Ian Bishop took three wickets each on Saturday as Victoria were bundled out for 197.
